reviews.text: Good service, nice stuff.

I’ve been taking my dog to 21 Pooch for about four years, and unfortunately, the experience has changed a lot from when we first started. For years, I trusted Valiera with my dog and always felt comfortable because she knew him, handled him well, and I knew who was grooming him.

Now it seems like there are constantly different groomers, and I haven’t been comfortable with how some of them handle the dogs. They can be rough, which is especially disappointing when you’ve trusted a business with your dog for years.

The pricing has also gotten ridiculous. It feels like there is an extra charge for every little thing now, including an additional fee if another groomer has to assist with something as basic as clipping your dog’s nails. At a certain point, all of these added fees make the service no longer worth the price.

It’s disappointing because this is literally the only grooming business my dog has ever been to, so I stayed loyal for a long time. But after seeing how much the service, staff consistency, and pricing have changed, I won’t be returning. I’ll be finding a new groomer where I can feel comfortable knowing who is handling my dog and where the pricing feels reasonable for the service being provided.

I am writing this review after a long time of hesitation, and I truly regret that I didn’t pay attention to the warning signs earlier.

When I came to this salon recently, I witnessed rough and careless treatment of a dog that was brought in just before my arrival. That moment made everything finally make sense to me.

I had been going to this salon for about two years, and during all this time my dog clearly showed fear. She does not want to enter the salon, refuses to get out of the car, pulls away from my hands, and on several occasions she even urinated from fear. Unfortunately, I didn’t take this seriously at first.

What makes this even more disturbing is that my dog is very calm by nature and actually enjoys grooming. In other grooming salons, the staff always said very kind things about her, and she was never afraid. She behaves perfectly during grooming elsewhere — no stress, no fear.

In addition, the quality of grooming here is very poor. Every visit feels like a gamble. One time the haircut looks acceptable, the next time it looks terrible. I will attach photos to show the results.
They also wash her badly — her stomach is often still dirty after the appointment.

After seeing how animals are treated there, I now fully understand why my dog was so scared.

I do not recommend this place and will never return.
I am truly sorry that I didn’t notice this earlier and continued bringing my dog here for so long.

The staff was very rude, both in their communication with people and animals.
This was the first time I saw my dog ​​unwilling to go to them, and instead of trying to coax him or communicate with him in any way, the groomer started dragging him by the leash (and even asked me to leave). I asked if they had any treats so I could give one to the groomer to entice my dog, but when I tried to take a treat from the jar, I pricked my finger. I don't know what it was, dried meat or bones sticking out of the treats, and I'm afraid to imagine how something so sharp could injure someone internally🤯
The groomer also insisted that I pick up the dog immediately after the service because they had a late fee policy and my dog ​​was the last one (but there was someone else getting a haircut when I arrived).
I felt terrible and didn't want to leave him there, but there's no waiting area, and all the windows are covered with opaque film so you can't see what the employees are doing, so we waited in the car.
When I came back and saw my dog ​​in the mirrors, he was trembling and lying on the floor in a cage without any blanket or bedding.
When I picked him up, the groomer continued to speak rudely and didn't say a word about how the service went.
Afterwards, at home, we examined him and his nails were terribly trimmed, as if the person had no idea how to do it. Many of his nails were split or simply damaged. He also developed an allergic reaction from the products (or from some treats they might have given him) – even though the employee assured me that they don't give any food unless it's agreed upon with the owner.

We used to go to their downtown branch and everything was always fine; he happily ran into the arms of the employees there, but this visit to this branch will be the last. I hope other clients will read this and think twice before going here.
